claim: The hard-coded digest 8e34fc298390875de416e6a4afcb8cabeceb25d9aa8506c1a2f9353cf702ea5f is the SHA-256 of the yq_linux_amd64 asset published in the mikefarah/yq v4.54.1 GitHub release, as the comment states.
source_excerpt:
# Digest published for yq_linux_amd64 in the v4.54.1 GitHub release.
# Update version and digest together after verifying the upstream asset.
VERSION=v4.54.1
SHA256=8e34fc298390875de416e6a4afcb8cabeceb25d9aa8506c1a2f9353cf702ea5f
verify_against: Upstream yq release metadata (checksums file / asset digest) for tag v4.54.1
verify_hint: Compare against the `checksums` / `checksums_hashes_order` assets of the mikefarah/yq v4.54.1 release for the `yq_linux_amd64` entry

claim: The download URL https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.54.1/yq_linux_amd64 is the correct asset path and resolves over HTTPS-only redirects as constrained by --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https'.
verify_against: mikefarah/yq release asset naming and GitHub release-download redirect behavior
verify_hint: Check the asset list for the mikefarah/yq v4.54.1 release and that GitHub's release download redirect chain to objects.githubusercontent.com is HTTPS-only

claim: RUNNER_TEMP and GITHUB_PATH are both set and writable inside a composite-action step, and appending a directory to GITHUB_PATH makes `yq` resolvable in later steps of the same job.
verify_against: GitHub Actions composite-action environment and GITHUB_PATH semantics
verify_hint: Check GitHub Actions docs for `RUNNER_TEMP`/`GITHUB_PATH` availability in `runs.using: composite` steps and the `Read config` steps in `.github/workflows/move-to-in-progress.yml` and `close-released-items.yml` that invoke `yq`

claim: `printf '%s  yq\n' "$SHA256" | sha256sum --check -` run from inside the download directory reads the file named `yq` relative to the cwd and exits non-zero on mismatch, so the install line is never reached.
verify_against: GNU coreutils sha256sum --check input format and exit codes
verify_hint: Check the coreutils `sha256sum --check` manual for the two-space digest/filename format, relative-path resolution and exit status on mismatch

claim: On a digest mismatch the installer's stderr contains the literal substring "did NOT match", as the test asserts.
verify_against: GNU coreutils sha256sum failure message wording (locale-dependent) on the CI runner image
verify_hint: Check the `sha256sum --check` mismatch message emitted by coreutils ("WARNING: 1 computed checksum did NOT match") and whether locale settings in the pytest environment can change it

claim: The stub `curl` reproduces the real curl invocation the installer makes: it scans argv for `--output` followed by the destination path and copies the fixture there, which matches the installer's actual flag ordering.
verify_hint: Compare the stub's argv scan against lines 12-14 of `.github/actions/install-yq/install.sh`, including whether `curl` is found via PATH rather than an absolute path

claim: Both workflow YAML documents expose a job keyed `config` whose `steps` list contains a step with `id: config` and a `run` string, and a step whose `uses` is exactly `./.github/actions/install-yq`.
verify_against: The parsed structure of .github/workflows/move-to-in-progress.yml and close-released-items.yml
verify_hint: Check the `jobs.config.steps` sections of both `.github/workflows/move-to-in-progress.yml` and `.github/workflows/close-released-items.yml` for the step `id: config` and the `uses` value

claim: `@anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2` exists on npm and its `pack <dir> <out>` subcommand accepts the same arguments as the previously unversioned CLI.
verify_against: The @anthropic-ai/mcpb package on npm (version 2.1.2 CLI surface)
verify_hint: Check that version 2.1.2 is published for `@anthropic-ai/mcpb` and that its `pack` command signature matches the invocation in `mcpb/build.sh`

claim: The README asserts packing uses @anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2, that the exact version must be updated in build.sh, and that the CLI's transitive npm dependencies are not locked.
source_excerpt:
Packing uses `@anthropic-ai/mcpb@2.1.2`. Update that exact version in `build.sh`
when adopting a new CLI release; its transitive npm dependencies are not locked.
verify_against: mcpb/build.sh and any other place that invokes the mcpb CLI (e.g. .github/workflows/mcpb.yml)
verify_hint: Check `mcpb/build.sh` for the pinned spec and grep for other `@anthropic-ai/mcpb` invocations (workflows, Dockerfile) that would falsify "Packing uses 2.1.2" or the single-place update instruction

claim: The CHANGELOG asserts the MCPB pack CLI is pinned and a fixed yq release is SHA-256-verified before installation in exactly the two legacy project-automation workflows.
source_excerpt:
- Pin the MCPB pack CLI and verify a fixed yq release against its SHA-256 digest
  before installation in the two legacy project-automation workflows. (#176, #237, #241)
verify_against: All workflows under .github/workflows/ that install or invoke yq
verify_hint: Grep `.github/workflows/` for `yq` installs to confirm only `move-to-in-progress.yml` and `close-released-items.yml` remain, i.e. no third workflow still fetches an unverified yq

claim: The composite action's description that it installs the pinned Linux amd64 yq release holds for every job that uses it, i.e. all callers run on a Linux amd64 runner.
source_excerpt: description: Install the pinned Linux amd64 yq release after SHA-256 verification
verify_against: The runs-on values of every job that uses ./.github/actions/install-yq
verify_hint: Check `jobs.config.runs-on` in `.github/workflows/move-to-in-progress.yml` and `.github/workflows/close-released-items.yml` against the amd64-only download in `install.sh`

claim: Appending $RUNNER_TEMP/sqllens-yq-bin to GITHUB_PATH suffices for the later `Read config` steps to resolve `yq`, which no longer exists at /usr/local/bin/yq as the removed install step provided.
verify_against: The ubuntu-latest runner image tool list and the installer's PATH export
verify_hint: Check whether the GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest image preinstalls `yq` elsewhere on PATH (which would mask the new install) and that the `Read config` step runs after the composite action in the same job

claim: `mktemp -d "$RUNNER_TEMP/yq-download.XXXXXX"` plus the EXIT trap removes the temporary directory on success, checksum failure and curl failure alike, including when RUNNER_TEMP contains spaces.
verify_against: Bash trap-on-EXIT semantics under `set -euo pipefail` and mktemp template requirements
verify_hint: Check that the EXIT trap fires for the errexit path of the `curl` and `sha256sum` lines, and compare with the cleanup assertion at the end of `test_yq_verification_precedes_install` in `tests/unit/test_build_inputs.py`
